title: Evals systems: scripts quick-reference and CI patterns
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact, executable-focused reference for onboarding model evals into our evals harness. It complements longer design docs by listing concrete script patterns, dataset loader idioms, scoring function templates, and CI wiring that reviewers and new onboarders can copy-paste.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied-ML engineers, infra engineers who wire CI, and solutions engineers validating regressions.
- Scope: small-to-medium eval suites (10s to low-100s of prompt examples), unit/smoke tests for model variants, and CI gating for PRs that touch loaders/scorers.

High-level goals:
- Fast, reproducible local iteration (dockerized runner invocation).
- Deterministic artifacts for baseline comparisons (report CSVs, per-example outputs).
- Lightweight CI that catches obvious regressions and enforces test fixtures.

Canonical repo layout (recommended):
- evals/
  - datasets/            # loader modules, fixtures, sample data (jsonl/parquet)
  - adapters/            # model adapters / small wrappers to call runtime/hosted API
  - scorers/             # scoring functions and utilities
  - scripts/             # helpers: run_eval.py, summarize.py, export_report.sh
  - ci/                  # CI smoke configs and local test harness

Example: minimal loader pattern (python) - loader should be deterministic and small:
- file: evals/datasets/simple_jsonl_loader.py
  - function: load_examples(path: str) -> List[Dict[str,str]]
  - behavior: stream JSONL, validate required fields (id, prompt, gold), optionally seed a shuffle for stress tests

Pseudo-code:
 def load_examples(path):
     with open(path) as f:
         for line in f:
             doc = json.loads(line)
             if not all(k in doc for k in ("id","prompt")):
                 raise ValueError("malformed example")
             yield {"id": str(doc["id"]), "prompt": doc["prompt"], "gold": doc.get("gold")}

Key loader patterns and tradeoffs:
- JSONL streaming loader: best for human-authored prompt sets, small memory, easy patching.
- Parquet/Arrow datasets: good for larger evals or when storing precomputed features (embedding vectors). Use pyarrow/dataset for sharded reading.
- S3-backed manifest: manifest file listing URIs. Loader must validate checksums or sizes for reproducibility.
- Fixture mode: include a tiny in-repo sample (<=20 examples) used by unit tests and CI smoke runs. This fixture SHOULD be deterministic and not hit external APIs.

Batched inference wrapper (adapter) tips:
- Expose a small interface: infer_batch(batch_prompts: List[str], config: Dict) -> List[outputs]
- Keep ordering stable: return outputs in the same order as inputs.
- Provide a mock adapter for local tests that returns canned responses.
- Support two execution modes via env var: LOCAL_MOCK=true and USE_HOSTED_API=true

Scoring functions (patterns):
- scorer contract: score_example(pred: str, gold: Optional[str], ctx: Dict) -> Dict[str, float | str]
  - must include: "score" (primary metric, numeric), "pass" (bool-ish string), and optionally "explanation"

Common scoring implementations:
1) exact_match (for short, canonical outputs)
   - normalize whitespace/case/punct, compare equality => score 1/0
2) normalized_f1 (for QA style outputs)
   - tokenize by whitespace, remove stop punctuation, compute F1 on token overlap
3) semantic_similarity (for open generation)
   - use cached embedding vectors for gold and pred, compute cosine similarity. Fall back to lexical metrics if embeddings missing.
4) likelihood_ratio scoring (for classification/regression calibration checks)
   - compute log-likelihood under candidate model vs baseline model, report delta_ll per-example and aggregated

Template (python) for scorer wrapper:
 def evaluate_example(pred, gold, example):
     metrics = {}
     metrics['exact_match'] = 1.0 if normalize(pred) == normalize(gold) else 0.0
     metrics['norm_f1'] = normalized_f1(pred, gold)
     metrics['pass'] = metrics['norm_f1'] > 0.8 or metrics['exact_match'] == 1.0
     return metrics

Regression report format (CSV/TSV recommended):
- Columns to include (as string column names):
  - example_id, prompt_hash, model_version, metric_primary, metric_secondary, delta_vs_baseline, pred_text_short, gold_text_short, notes
- Always write a per-example JSONL artifact in addition to the tabular CSV; JSONL should contain full model output and diagnostics (logprobs, raw tokens, embeddings refs).

Statistical checks and thresholds:
- Use bootstrap CI for aggregated metric deltas (n=2000 bootstrap samples by default). Flag a regression if: p_value < 0.05 AND delta_primary_metric < -0.5% (absolute depending on metric).
- Practical rules: for high variance tasks (open generation), require a larger delta (e.g., -2%) or manual review.

CI wiring (GitHub Actions example - high level):
- workflow: evals-on-pr.yml (trigger: pull_request for paths under evals/**)
- stages:
  - unit_tests: run dataset loader tests and scorer unit tests against fixture data (fast; must pass).
  - smoke_inference: run a tiny eval (fixture) with mock adapter and with a short call to real runtime if COMMITTER_APPROVED==true. Limit to 5s per example.
  - integration_report: when a PR sets label 'run-full-eval', kick off a longer job on a runner with GPUs or ephemeral cloud GPUs. This job writes artifacts to S3 and posts a summary link on the PR.

GH Actions job snippet (pseudo):
 jobs:
   unit_tests:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - checkout
       - setup-python
       - pip install -r requirements.txt
       - python -m pytest evals/datasets/test_loader.py::test_fixture_loader

 gating rules (recommended):
 - PRs that change scaffolding (files under evals/adapters or evals/scorers) must pass unit_tests AND smoke_inference.
 - Larger metric-impacting changes (any code that touches scoring or aggregation) must be accompanied by a regression report (CSV + JSONL) comparing new vs baseline and be manually reviewed by at least one applied-ml engineer.

Artifact storage and naming conventions:
- s3://evals-artifacts/{repo}/{pr_number}/{model_version}/report-{timestamp}.csv
- include metadata.json next to CSV with keys: commit_sha, pr_number, runtime_config, baseline_commit (optional)

Command-line runner examples:
- local quick run (mock):
  EXPORT_MOCK=true python evals/scripts/run_eval.py --dataset evals/datasets/fixtures/small.jsonl --adapter evals/adapters/mock_adapter --out report.jsonl
- reproducible run against hosted runtime (CI/integration runner):
  python evals/scripts/run_eval.py --dataset s3://manifests/pr-142-manifest.json --adapter adapters/hosted_adapter --batch-size 8 --out s3://evals-artifacts/…/report.jsonl

Best practices / gotchas:
- Always include a tiny in-repo fixture that exercises loaders and scorers. CI should rely on it for fast feedback.
- Keep scoring primitives pure functions to ease unit testing. Avoid side effects in scorers.
- Cache expensive ops (embeddings, tokenization) during offline eval runs; include cache version in metadata.
- When comparing against a baseline commit, record both commits and the exact artifact paths so we can reproduce the delta.
- For open-generation metrics, store several metrics (lexical, semantic, human-sim proxies) rather than a single number.

Sample checklist for onboarding a new eval (quick):
- [ ] Add loader under evals/datasets and include a small fixture.
- [ ] Implement adapter stub + mock adapter.
- [ ] Implement scorer with unit tests.
- [ ] Add workflow in .github/workflows/evals-on-pr.yml if new files are added.
- [ ] Run full eval locally, produce CSV + JSONL artifacts, and upload to S3 (or attach to PR).
- [ ] Attach regression report to PR and tag reviewers from eng-applied-ml.

Diagnostics and debugging tips:
- When a metric is noisy, inspect per-example deltas and examples with largest negative delta. Often failures cluster by prompt template or tokenization mismatch.
- If CI fails intermittently on integration runs, capture and upload docker/runner logs and set a rerun-once policy for flaky infra.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide a canonical micro-benchmark dataset for latency/throughput numbers for adapter changes (file: ci/latency-benchmark-plan.md).
- Formalize alert thresholds for small-sample evals (n<100).
- Add a standard Visual Diff artifact for per-example text diffs (html) so reviewers can browse changes quickly.

References and quick links:
- Confluence onboarding checklist: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/ML/Eval+Onboarding+Checklist
- Example CI PR that showed a delta workflow: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-harness/pull/142
- Jira ticket for gating policy discussion: ML-578

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally concise and operational. If you are onboarding a new eval, follow the checklist and copy the loader/scorer templates verbatim; adapt edge-case handling only after unit tests are added.
- If you update scoring behavior, add a changelog entry under evals/CHANGELOG.md describing the rationale and expected metric shifts.

Signed-off-by: Aisha Patel (eng-applied-ml)
